meaning: Cannot start, act, or orient within 60 seconds.
example: Tester asks where to type or what game this is.
default_action: Fix navigation/copy before recruiting more testers.

meaning: Opening promises facts/choices but user cannot tell which are binding.
example: Tester treats a suggestion as a hard rule.
default_action: Expose opening invariant/choice boundary in human language.

meaning: System ignores, overrides, or repeatedly re-asks after a player decline.
example: Quest is accepted after player walks away.

meaning: Inventory, identity, location, or canon contradicts earlier accepted fact.
example: Item works despite absent ledger state.

meaning: Outcome critical to play cannot be explained or receipt does not match state.
A player correction does not survive later turns or reload.
Kid/safety boundary leaks prohibited content or dead-ends player.
example: Mode returns graphic harm after redirect.
default_action: Block release; invoke kill switch if live.

meaning: Mode selection/setup obscures first meaningful turn.
example: Tester spends more than five minutes configuring.
default_action: Simplify defaults and defer advanced settings.

meaning: Truth exists but is not visible or cannot be located.
example: Tester cannot tell why marker exists.

meaning: Voice change changes game facts, math, safety, or player identity.
Player enjoys prose but cannot articulate unique reason to return/pay.
Latency or retry behavior breaks agency/understanding.
Readability, contrast, keyboard, motion, or screen-reader flow blocks play.
Cosmetic/wording issue does not alter trust, safety, or task completion.
example: One label unclear but workaround obvious.
